newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat gains on AWB pool estimate rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat gains on AWB pool estimate rise.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose in thin volume on Tuesday after the Australian Wheat Board on Monday raised its 1996/97 pool return estimate by A$4 a tonne for most grades, taking Australian Standard White (ASW) to A$192 a tonne.
The spot March contract rose A$3 a tonne to A$169 in an overnight trade of three 50-tonne lots while near May rose A$6.50 to A$170.50 a tonne on a volume of 10 contracts.
"The increase in the pool price pushed the market up," Ben Suttie of C A and L Bell Commodities Pty Ltd said.
The way the Chicago market was trending - down - the weakness of the Australian dollar was the only reason the AWB could offer a higher pool price, Suttie said.
He said he expected the first 1997/98 pool estimate to be announced soon to show a decline of A$10 to A$20 a tonne.
The AWB said on Monday it would announce its first 1997/98 pool estimate on February 17.
Suttie also noted that most of the 23 million tonne 1996/97 Australian wheat crop had gone into the AWB pool for export , leaving the domestic market quite tight, which is why it was holding up.
